chunk_findings.detail: `mark_missed_final` decides whether a reviewer missed the final commit by comparing the raw strings `reviewed_head` and `final_head`, while `_review_clause` later prints both hashes truncated to 7 characters. If `final_head` is an abbreviated commit identifier that is a prefix of the full `reviewed_head` (a normal Git short SHA), the raw comparison fails and sets `missed_final`, but the rendered note shows the same 7-character string for both. For example, with `review_rounds = {"reviewed_head": "abc1234567890", ...}` and `mark_missed_final(..., "abc1234")`, the report says `reviewer did not see the final commit (reviewed abc1234, final abc1234)`, which is wrong because the reviewer did cover the final commit.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/report_gates.py:mark_missed_final (and ddflow/services/report_render.py:_review_clause)

chunk_findings.detail: The new guard compares only the first 7 characters of the two SHAs, so it can fail to mark a genuinely missed final commit. Given a row with `review_rounds={"reviewed_head": "abc1234" + "0" * 33}` and `final_head="abc1234" + "1" * 33`, both are full commit identifiers for different commits, but `reviewed_head[:7] == final_head[:7]`, so `missed_final` is not set and the report omits the “reviewer did not see the final commit” note even though the reviewer did not see the final commit. The comparison should preserve full SHA identity (or use a proper prefix check for abbreviations) instead of a fixed 7-char slice.

chunk_findings.detail: `rounds = [_review_line(g) for g in d["gates"] if g.get("review_rounds")]` only checks whether `review_rounds` is present/truthy. A gate row such as `{"gate": "rubber_duck", "outcome": "passed", "review_rounds": {"used": 0, "max": 4, "refutation": False}}` passes that guard, so `_review_line` returns `rubber_duck 0/4` and `lines` emits a `review rounds: rubber_duck 0/4` line even though no review rounds were spent and there was no refutation. This contradicts the function’s stated behavior and the intent to report only gates that spent rounds or passed on refutation, producing a false user-facing report line.
